item.title: How OpenAI’s Rogue A.I. Agents Tried to Trick a Robot Detector

item.title: Anthropic’s Blacklisting by the Pentagon Was Legal, Federal Judges Rule

item.media:description: Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei.

item.title: Google Is Sending an A.I. Data Center to Outer Space
item.description: Next Thursday, Google is sending an experimental satellite into orbit that will have enough computing power to answer simple A.I. queries from space.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger and Cade Metz
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: A technician in a clean room at the Planet Labs office inspects the solar panels and wires of a Google-commissioned satellite before a vibration test meant to mimic the shaking it will undergo during launch.

item.title: TikTok to Pay Alabama $100 Million to Settle Social Media Addiction Claims
item.description: The settlement, which also includes changes to the platform’s features, is the latest in a string of agreements by companies to address child addiction.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang
item.media:credit: Robyn Beck/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: TikTok’s settlement with Alabama could cost the company up to $300 million if it fails to meet the terms of the agreement.

item.title: Is China Really Stealing A.I. From American Companies?

item.title: Elizabeth Holmes to Transfer to Halfway House in August 2027
item.description: The founder of the blood-testing start-up Theranos was sentenced to 11 years in prison for fraud and had been serving time at a minimum-security federal prison in Texas.
item.dc:creator: Erin Griffith
item.media:credit: Go Nakamura/Reuters
item.media:description: The Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, who was convicted of fraud in 2022 and sentenced to 11 years behind bars, is expected to be transferred to a halfway house next August.

item.title: OpenAI’s A.I. Tried Breaching Four Other Targets, With No Prompting
item.description: In each incident, the technology appeared to be conducting mundane data collection and resorted to hacking techniques to get it, researchers said.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger and Victoria Kim
item.media:credit: Lucas Foglia for The New York Times
item.media:description: OpenAI’s offices in San Francisco. At least four times this year, the company’s artificial intelligence hacked or tried to break into government and university websites without being instructed to do so.

item.title: America’s A.I. Leaders Warn U.N. of Possible Peril Absent a Global Response
